description: MirrorMe on the cluster: the relay, the group service and the Discord manager. The top rows read the kubelet and the node agent; the rows below read the relay's and the group service's own metrics listeners. A panel with no data names something that does not exist at the moment: no group, no stream, no kick. The Logs row carries warnings and errors; the whole stream, organized per container, is the MirrorMe Logs dashboard.

panels.description: Available against desired. One replica by design: the media legs are host ports and two pods cannot hold the same ones, so a rollout recreates rather than overlaps.
panels.title: Replicas

panels.description: Summed over the four containers, each counted once whatever pod carried it. The relay restarting takes every stream with it.
panels.title: Restarts

panels.description: Into the pod's interface. Every media leg is a host port the node forwards here, so this carries the publishers and the proxy's traffic together.
panels.title: Ingress

panels.description: Out of the pod's interface, which is the leg the VPS pays for.
panels.title: Egress

panels.description: Egress over ingress. One publisher watched by three reads 3, and the figure is what turns a publish bitrate into an uplink bill. An idle pod reads near 1 on housekeeping traffic alone.
panels.title: Fan-out

panels.description: Against the pod's limits together. The relay holds three of the node's four cores because what it costs is the streams on it, and nothing in the manifest decides how many that is.
panels.title: CPU

panels.description: Working set against the pod's limits together.
panels.title: Memory
Traffic and resources, from the kubelet and the node agent

panels.description: Both legs on one axis, so the gap between them is the fan-out. The kubelet counts bytes at the pod's interface and knows nothing about which stream or which member they belong to.
panels.title: Pod ingress and egress

panels.description: The node's own counters, one series per interface and direction. eth0 is the public address clients reach; tailscale0 is the tunnel the node joined the cluster over, so cluster traffic and media traffic are separable here and nowhere else.
panels.title: Node interfaces

panels.description: Usage is the pod's, the limit the three containers' together. The kubelet reports no per-container usage, so which of the three is spending it is not a question this reading answers.
panels.title: CPU against the pod's limits

panels.description: Working set is what the kubelet would evict on. RSS beside it is what the processes hold.
panels.title: Memory against the pod's limits
Groups and members, from the group service's metrics listener

panels.description: One bar per group holding a lease. A group is named by its prefix, the base32 a key derives, which is the one name the relay and the group service share.
panels.title: Members per group

panels.description: One row per member holding a live lease. The name is the one the app stated. The member id the relay logs a connection under is a keyed digest of it and never leaves the group.
panels.title: Who is connected

panels.description: The three counts on one axis. A member count climbing while the group count holds is a group filling up; both climbing is a second group starting.
panels.title: Groups, members and publishers
Streams and transports, from the relay's metrics listener

panels.description: Relay paths carrying a track. A path something connected to but has not established a track on is not ready and is not counted.
panels.title: Live streams

panels.description: Every connection the relay holds, publish and read alike, across all of its listeners.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Summed over the relay's own path counters. Below the pod reading above it is the proxy and the housekeeping the relay does not see.
panels.title: Ingress, as the relay counts it

panels.description: Summed over the relay's own path counters, which attribute the bytes to a stream where the pod's interface cannot.
panels.title: Egress, as the relay counts it

panels.description: Which listener the bytes leave through. The TLS and cleartext listeners of one protocol are summed into the one transport name the app uses, the split readerKinds already carries.
panels.title: Egress by transport

panels.description: A viewer reconnecting on its own shows here as a step down and back up.
panels.title: Connections by transport

panels.description: One line per publisher, times the viewers reading it. A stream nobody watches costs nothing here however high its ingress.
panels.title: Egress per stream

panels.description: SRT is the default publish transport and the one leg no proxy wraps, so a bad uplink reads here before a viewer reports a stutter.
panels.title: SRT packets lost

panels.description: The relay configures one wildcard path, so a path listed here is one something connected to. Readers is the relay's own count of who is reading it, which is the closest thing to an audience that does not go through the group service. A path under public/ is outside membership: no key derives that prefix and anybody may read it.
panels.title: Paths the relay carries
Membership enforcement, from the group service's metrics listener

panels.description: Whether both metrics listeners answered their last scrape. The relay counts bytes and connections; only the group service knows which member holds one, so a dark half of this dashboard is one of these being down.
panels.title: Exporters

panels.description: A close the relay would not carry out. Each is a member whose lease lapsed and who is possibly still watching, which is why it is not folded into the count of what was closed.
panels.title: Kicks refused (1h)

panels.description: A per-protocol list a sweep could not read, so that sweep saw fewer connections than exist. Same consequence as a refused kick and counted apart from it.
panels.title: Lists unread (1h)

panels.description: A run of refusals is somebody holding a key this deployment does not sign for.
panels.title: Tokens refused (1h)

panels.description: What enforcement takes off the relay, by the list the kick went to. A sweep runs on every membership change and on every read, so a flat line with members leaving is a sweep that is not finding them.
panels.title: Connections closed

panels.description: Leases stated, released and lapsed. A release is an app that closed. A lapse is one that stopped refreshing, which a crash and a dead network look identical from here.
panels.title: Lease churn

panels.description: Warnings and errors from all four containers: [WARN] and [ERROR] from groupd and discordd, WAR and ERR from the relay, level warn and error from the proxy, plus any Go traceback.
